_about: Regression gate for npm run bench -- --assert (E2E Testing Strategy §3.7, ticket YDuDawBIoLKuPRK0uCMO). Re-baselined 19 Oct 2026 (ticket IqAdH5i8jWIGNElQR135) from `npm run bench -- --calibrate` at 82163ae plus that ticket's change, on a 4 vCPU / 16 GB cloud sandbox; before that, seeded from the 24 Sep 2026 scale review and last changed 3 Oct (81a1947d). rps must stay above threshold × (1 − tolerance); ms must stay below threshold × (1 + tolerance). A deliberate change updates this file in the same PR; changing it changes the nightly's cache key, so CI recalibrates on its next run. `--calibrate` writes bench/baseline.local.json (git-ignored) from the machine, which --assert then prefers. Since 8 Oct (f11bb1f7) every synthetic slot is one private-auction deal and bids go to 3 windows, so shapes C and T send only 1,020-1,206 bids and POST /v1/reservations is now measured over the time the bids took (bench/rate.ts), not --seconds. Moved by more than 25% against the 3 Oct file, with the reason: POST /v1/reservations in all four shapes (992-1,035 → 546-608 req/s): the 8 Oct workload, each bid now a deal bid over 3 windows; GET /v1/inventory page of 50 (35-51 → 99-126 ms p50, 582-850 → 231-255 req/s) and ?status=available (1 yr) (62-83 → 266-301 ms p50; B, C, T 384-502 → 97-107 req/s) and GET /admin/v1/booking-schedule, default and 92 d (A 4,374 → 9,450 and 26,378 → 38,820 ms; B 475 → 969; C 170 → 341 and 659 → 826; T 170 → 307 and 659 → 997 ms): the 8 Oct workload (every slot one deal) and the sandbox, which ran about 2× slower than the 3 Oct runner on the unchanged read paths; availability (7 d) and (1 yr) and GET /v1/inventory/{id} rose (2,187-2,347 → 3,480-4,128 req/s; 1 yr 672-704 → 2,740-3,446): the 8 Oct deal-only estate has fewer open windows to resolve, not a code change; C/T Available Inventory 59 → 96-105 ms (43 → 58 ms between 771cf9eb and f01c8ba1, cause not pinned); C auction 460 → 612 ms and B billing one window 370 → 189 ms, A billing tick 77 → 55 ms: run-to-run noise on a different machine. A's and B's Available Inventory thresholds (1836 and 213 ms) were deliberately NOT raised: after the one-list-per-playlist fix they must pass as committed.
